Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

The patch modifies a single file, `drivers/android/binder/thread.rs`, to fix a bug where an empty file descriptor array (FDA) with zero length caused an out-of-bounds error. The core change replaces a struct-based representation with an enum, eliminating a previous ambiguity where a `skip` value of zero was used as a sentinel to distinguish between a pointer fixup (`binder_buffer_object`) and an FDA skip (`binder_fd_array_object`). Since zero is also a valid skip length for an empty FDA, this led to incorrect handling.

**Modifications in `drivers/android/binder/thread.rs`**:

- The `PointerFixupEntry` struct (containing `skip`, `pointer_value`, `target_offset`) is replaced with an enum `PointerFixupEntry` having two variants:
  - `Fixup` – holds `pointer_value` and `target_offset`, used for `binder_buffer_object` fixups (previously indicated by `skip == 0`).
  - `Skip` – holds `skip` and `target_offset`, used for `binder_fd_array_object` skips (`skip` is the number of bytes to skip).
- All places that create `PointerFixupEntry` instances are updated to use the appropriate enum variant. In `translate_object`, the push for a pointer fixup now uses `PointerFixupEntry::Fixup` (removing the zero `skip`), and the push for an FDA skip uses `PointerFixupEntry::Skip` (removing the unused `pointer_value`).
- In `apply_sg`, the logic that previously checked `fixup.skip == 0` to decide between writing a pointer or skipping bytes is replaced by pattern matching on the enum. The `fixup_len` and `fixup_offset` are extracted from the variant, and the pointer write is only performed for `Fixup` variants.
- All associated variable names and method calls are adjusted accordingly (e.g., extracting `pointer_value` from `Fixup` instead of the struct field).

**Relationships between modifications**:
All changes are confined to a single file and represent a refactoring of the `PointerFixupEntry` data structure and its usage. The primary relationship is that the enum-based design explicitly separates the two fixup types, removing the implicit semantic meaning of `skip == 0`. This ensures that an FDA with zero length (where `skip == 0`) is correctly treated as a skip with zero bytes, rather than being misinterpreted as a pointer fixup. The logical flow in `apply_sg` is preserved but now uses structured pattern matching, preventing the out-of-bounds access that occurred when an empty FDA at the end of the buffer incorrectly triggered a pointer write.

Here is the commit message:
rust_binder: correctly handle FDA objects of length zero

Fix a bug where an empty FDA (fd array) object with 0 fds would cause an
out-of-bounds error. The previous implementation used `skip == 0` to
mean "this is a pointer fixup", but 0 is also the correct skip length
for an empty FDA. If the FDA is at the end of the buffer, then this
results in an attempt to write 8-bytes out of bounds. This is caught and
results in an EINVAL error being returned to userspace.

The pattern of using `skip == 0` as a special value originates from the
C-implementation of Binder. As part of fixing this bug, this pattern is
replaced with a Rust enum.

I considered the alternate option of not pushing a fixup when the length
is zero, but I think it's cleaner to just get rid of the zero-is-special
stuff.

The root cause of this bug was diagnosed by Gemini CLI on first try. I
used the following prompt:

> There appears to be a bug in @drivers/android/binder/thread.rs where
> the Fixups oob bug is triggered with 316 304 316 324. This implies
> that we somehow ended up with a fixup where buffer A has a pointer to
> buffer B, but the pointer is located at an index in buffer A that is
> out of bounds. Please investigate the code to find the bug. You may
> compare with @drivers/android/binder.c that implements this correctly.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: DeepChirp <DeepChirp@outlook.com>
Closes: https://github.com/waydroid/waydroid/issues/2157
Fixes: eafedbc7c050 ("rust_binder: add Rust Binder driver")
Tested-by: DeepChirp <DeepChirp@outlook.com>
Signed-off-by: Alice Ryhl <aliceryhl@google.com>
Acked-by: Carlos Llamas <cmllamas@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251229-fda-zero-v1-1-58a41cb0e7ec@google.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The previous implementation used `skip == 0` as a sentinel to indicate a pointer fixup (for binder_buffer_object) while also using `skip` to represent the number of bytes to skip for an FDA fixup. However, an empty FDA has a skip of 0, which is indistinguishable from a pointer fixup. This caused an empty FDA at the end of a buffer to be incorrectly treated as a pointer fixup, leading to an out-of-bounds write of 8 bytes (the size of a u64 pointer) beyond the buffer.
